correctness.rationale: Reviewed RESULT.md:3–48, VERIFICATION.md and verify_square_index_patterns.py. The indicator in x contributes 16 for a matching word with all arguments nonzero, at most 8 for each of at most eight inputs having a zero argument, and at most 16 for the excluded x=0. For any nonempty subset of the four distinct nonzero shifts at p>=5, the product of the quadratic factors is squarefree: each root is simple and the factors have no shared root. The quadratic Weil bound gives (2|S|−1)sqrt(p) for the character sum, with coefficients totaling 49, so 16N_p^×>=p−49sqrt(p)−80. At 2579, (2579−80)^2>49^2*2579 and 2579−80>0; the lower bound increases thereafter. Independent replay: python3 /workspace/branches/replay_frozen_review.py 1 uses trial division, a residue table from successive odd differences of squares and scans the cyclic windows rejecting zeros. It exhausts all 373 primes 5<=p<2579, reproducing the exact 24 primes and their missing-word counts and the full mask fingerprint ae46170c708cc49792a01577a3ce855d0f2c54dda0f6a570596d42045a6d44aa. At 193 the mask is 0x7fff, at 197 it is 0xffff, and at 5 no valid window remains. The enumeration and proven tail together establish the classification, including that 197 is the first prime after the last exception.

originality.rationale: The exact exception list is mechanically recoverable from a prior complete finite six-word support generator and its proved infinite tail. An accepted square-start four-sign word is exactly an R-leading nonwrapping five-word; for p>=7 its occurrence is equivalent to occurrence as either the five-prefix or five-suffix of an occurring six-word. The earlier six-word record's published checker computes the full 64-bit support at all odd primes below 16384, including every bridge prime, and its theorem gives full support at p>=461. Project both ends, keep the R-leading words, and handle the empty case p=5. This yields the entire claimed prime-to-mask classification, not merely a large-prime existence statement. Separately, Buchaev–Tsfasman's July 2026 Theorem 2 already gives exact multiplicities for all these five-words. The decimal cutoff/list need not have been printed for the prior coverage to be decisive.
residual_risks: The exact cutoff 197 and full explicit list were not located verbatim in the compared works. The failure rests on demonstrable coverage and extraction, not on a claim that they were printed or on unresolved access to earlier sources.
